correctness.rationale: Explicit 11-vertex edge rule identifies the graph; all Hamiltonian paths have endpoints on the six degree-three-side vertices, with exactly four legal backbites. One exhaustive DFS enumerates exactly 222 unoriented paths; a separate check of all C(18,10)=43758 edge subsets recovers the same count and graph using a different edge-exchange criterion. Both construct 444 backbite edges and verify all-source BFS distances, eccentricity counts, exact histogram, explicit diameter-nine witness and disjoint diameter pairs; a separate subset dynamic program checks endpoint multiplicities. All computations are finite, complete and reproducible from embedded standalone programs.

value.rationale: The smallest non-Hamiltonian polyhedral graph is a canonical sparse 3-connected example outside squared-path sufficiency hypotheses. Complete backbite connectedness with a sharp nine-step bound answers a natural exact local-reconfiguration problem, while endpoint orbit multiplicities and the twelve disjoint extremal pairs reveal structure useful as a test case for path sampling/reconfiguration; the claim does not rely on unproven generalizations.
